Despite its name, Arab Light crude is not really a light crude. (Why are oil markets so darn confusing?)

So please don't think we can replace Arab Light directly with other light sweet crudes. The lower residue yield from the lighter crudes will be insufficient to load up the secondary units such as the FCC or cokers.

These grades from the attached chart are more suitable.

To take the lighter grades (like WTI and CPC), some blending will be required with heavier grades.

More details in the report link below.

Although the US-Iran war attracts most attention in the oil market, two important developments on the Russia-Ukraine war: 

1) Further fighting overnight (including strikes against refineries) seems to confirm that the energy truce is only happening in Donald Trump’s mind. 

2) US Congress passed legislation (with multiple Democrats supporting it) that would allow Trump to impose up to 100% tariffs on nations buying Russia crude (read here India and China). New Delhi issued overnight its protest.

CHART OF THE DAY: Venezuelan crude is flowing into the US at the highest rate since mid-2017, with imports surging to nearly 800,000 barrels a day last week. https://t.co/Q6qEIPobsw

U.S. REFINERS processed an average of 17.4 million barrels per day of crude and other feedstocks over the seven days ending on September 11. Processing was almost 0.5 million b/d higher than at the same point in 2025 and 2024 as refiners captured near-record margins and sought to offset the global shortage of gasoline and especially diesel. Processing was the fastest for the time of year since before the pandemic in 2019, despite a reduction in capacity, which resulted in exceptionally high rates of utilisation above 96%:

FT:

Global crude markets are tightening at what analysts at Energy Aspects described this week as an “eye-watering pace”, as buyers rush to make up for curtailed Saudi supplies. The consultancy said the market was short of about 5mn barrels a day of crude and refined fuels and that it expected prices to spiral upwards.

For much of this year, China has sought to cushion the impact of the war by cutting imports, drawing down stockpiles and raising retail prices to curtail demand. Its actions have helped shield countries around the world from even higher crude prices. 

But now China was “coming back off its crash diet”, said Bob McNally, founder of Rapidan Energy Group. He said China’s return to buying oil on the open market, the closure of the Saudi pipeline and the lack of a quick resolution to the war had combined to spark the surge in crude prices.

Germany’s renewable-energy developers are entering a shakeout after years of rapid expansion, with worsening project economics pushing a growing number into financial distress.

Hamburg-based solar developer Enerparc AG, one of Europe’s largest solar park operators, filed for insolvency this month with around €3 billion ($3.5 billion) of debt across the group. That follows the insolvency of wind developer Sowitec Group GmbH, while others including BayWa r.e. and ABO Energy have embarked on restructuring efforts. https://t.co/Wvo8LQy2tH
